gaps.sentence: Such ___ the demand for tickets that the website crashed.
gaps.explanation: Such was the demand that… — emphatic result structure.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ the chances of success be improved by patience.
gaps.explanation: Little will the chances be improved… — inversion with future.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets expensive, but they were also sold out.
gaps.explanation: Not only were the tickets… — inversion with 'be' needs no auxiliary.

gaps.sentence: Only when she apologised ___ he agree to meet again.
gaps.explanation: Only when she apologised did he agree — inversion.

gaps.sentence: Among the guests ___ the ambassador and her staff.
gaps.hint: fronted 'among' — verb agrees with later subject
gaps.explanation: Among the guests were the ambassador and her staff — verb before subject.

gaps.sentence: ___ the second half begin than the rain returned.
gaps.explanation: No sooner did the second half begin than… — inversion with do-support.

gaps.sentence: ___ it not been for your help, we would have failed.
gaps.explanation: Had it not been for = if it hadn't been for — fixed inverted conditional.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ they know that the deal had already collapsed.
gaps.explanation: Little did they know = they had no idea — emphatic idiom with inversion.
